sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the February 2026 Class Health Care Support Assistant College Final Exam, Cicely McDonnell College of Health Sciences (12 August 2026), Multiple Choice Questions Q48 to Q67. Q1 to Q7 are not included because page 2 of the paper was not available.

questions.text: A grieving relative says, "This cannot be happening. The doctors must be wrong." This is most consistent with:
questions.explanation: Denial (B) is correct because in Kübler-Ross's stages of grief, denial is a defence in which the person refuses to accept the reality of the loss ("this cannot be happening"). Acceptance (A) is coming to terms with the loss, depression (C) is sadness and withdrawal, and bargaining (D) is trying to make deals ("if only").

questions.text: A dying terminally ill patient develops noisy respiratory secretions. The HCA should:

options.A: Become anxious and tell the family the patient is suffering
options.B: Report to the nurse and provide appropriate comfort measures
options.C: Suction the patient to remove the secretions
options.D: Perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation to the patient immediately

questions.explanation: Report to the nurse and provide appropriate comfort measures (B) is correct because noisy breathing (the death rattle) is common near the end of life, is usually more distressing for the family than for the patient, and is managed by the nurse with positioning (side-lying), mouth care and prescribed drugs, and by explaining to the family. Showing anxiety (A) alarms the family, suctioning (C) is usually not helpful and is outside the HCA's role, and CPR (D) is not appropriate in a dying patient unless it is ordered.

questions.text: When communicating with a person who has a hearing impairment, the HCA should:

options.B: Face the person and speak clearly

questions.explanation: Face the person and speak clearly (B) is correct because facing the person lets them see your lips and facial expressions and speaking clearly at a normal pace with good lighting helps them understand. Shouting (A) distorts the sound and is disrespectful, reducing communication (C) isolates the patient, and a low tone (D) is harder to hear, since many hearing-impaired people lose high pitches first, but low, slow, clear speech is better than high pitch.

questions.text: A patient with cerebral palsy requires assistance with bathing. The patient can wash their face and upper body independently. The HCA should:

options.A: Complete the entire bath without involving the patient
options.B: Encourage the patient to perform the tasks they can safely manage
options.C: Encourage the patient to perform the entire bath
options.D: Ask a relative to help in performing the bed bath

questions.explanation: Encourage the patient to perform the tasks they can safely manage (B) is correct because care should promote independence, dignity and self-esteem, so the patient washes the face and upper body while the HCA helps with the parts they cannot reach. Doing everything for the patient (A) takes away independence. Expecting the entire bath (C) is unsafe, and asking a relative to help (D) is unnecessary.

questions.text: A 10 year old patient with Down syndrome is being assisted with personal care. The HCA should:

options.A: Speak to the patient's guardian instead of the patient
options.B: Adapt communication to their level of understanding
options.C: Make all choices for the patient

questions.explanation: Adapt communication to their level of understanding (B) is correct because the child is spoken to directly, using simple words, short sentences, demonstration and time to respond, which respects the child's dignity and encourages cooperation. The guardian is involved but should not replace the child (A). Making all choices (C) and ignoring preferences (D) take away the child's rights.

questions.text: Older adults are at increased risk of pressure injuries because of:
questions.explanation: Reduced mobility (B) is correct because when older adults move less, pressure stays on bony areas for long and blocks blood supply to the skin, causing pressure injuries. With ageing the skin becomes thinner (not thicker, so A is wrong), circulation decreases (not increases, so C is wrong), and muscle mass is lost (not gained, so D is wrong).

questions.text: The most important principle when providing care to an elderly person is to:

options.C: Make all decisions for the patient

questions.explanation: Provide person-centred care (B) is correct because care is built around the person's needs, preferences, values and dignity, and involves them in decisions. Promoting dependence (A) and making all decisions for the patient (C) remove independence, and focusing only on physical illness (D) ignores emotional, social and spiritual needs.

questions.text: An 82-year-old patient with dementia repeatedly tries to get out of bed at night. The most appropriate action is to:

options.A: Restrain the patient immediately in the bed and warn them not to come out
options.B: Assess the reason for the behaviour and implement appropriate safety measures
options.C: Delegate to the relative to restrain the patient at the bed at night
options.D: Allow the patient to have their wish

questions.explanation: Assess the reason for the behaviour and implement appropriate safety measures (B) is correct because wandering and restlessness often have a cause such as pain, hunger, a need to use the toilet, fear or an unfamiliar place, and measures such as a low bed, bed alarm, night light, toileting and calm reassurance are used. Restraint (A, C) is a last resort, can harm the patient and violates their rights. Simply allowing the patient to do as they wish (D) risks falls.

questions.text: The scope of the HCA's practice includes:
questions.explanation: Taking and documenting vital signs (B) is correct because measuring and recording temperature, pulse, respiration and blood pressure, and reporting abnormal results to the nurse, is within the HCA's scope. Giving intravenous drugs (A), counselling depressed patients (C) and assisting surgeons in theatre (D) require specialised training and professional registration.

questions.text: Unwritten rules, behaviors and expectations in a group or society are:
questions.explanation: Norms (B) is correct because norms are the unwritten rules and expected behaviours that guide how members of a group or society act. Principles (A) are fundamental guiding rules or truths, morals (C) are beliefs about right and wrong, and values (D) are the beliefs and ideals considered important.

questions.text: The ethical principle that requires the HCA to keep promises made to the patient is:
questions.explanation: Fidelity (A) is correct because fidelity means being faithful and keeping promises and commitments to patients. Veracity (B) is telling the truth, confidentiality (C) is protecting private information, and non-maleficence (D) is avoiding harm.

questions.text: A HCA administers a subcutaneous injection of insulin to a patient who had declined the injection. The HCA is liable for:
questions.explanation: Battery (C) is correct because battery is unlawful physical contact with a person without their consent; giving an injection to a patient who refused it is battery. Assault (B) is a threat or attempt to touch without consent, without the contact itself. Libel (A) is a written false statement that harms reputation, and invasion of privacy (D) is a breach of confidentiality or personal space.

questions.text: Which of the following is classified as a 'High-Alert' medication?
questions.explanation: Insulin (D) is correct because high-alert medications carry a higher risk of serious harm if used wrongly, and insulin can cause severe low blood sugar if the dose is wrong, so it needs double checking. Other examples are anticoagulants (heparin, Clexane), opioids and concentrated potassium. Antacids (A), saline nasal spray (B) and multivitamins (C) are low-risk.

questions.text: The principle of drug administration being exercised when a HCA checks the patient's wristband before giving a drug is:
questions.explanation: Right patient (A) is correct because checking the wristband (and asking the patient to state their name) confirms identity so that the drug is given to the correct person. Right drug (B) is checked against the prescription and label, right time (C) against the schedule, and right dose (D) against the prescription.

questions.text: A drug preparation for administration through the rectum is:
questions.explanation: Suppository (A) is correct because a suppository is a solid cone-shaped drug inserted into the rectum, where it melts and is absorbed. A pessary (B) is inserted into the vagina, and capsules and pills (C, D) are taken by mouth.

questions.text: Side effects of steroids include:
questions.explanation: Reduced immunity (C) is correct because steroids suppress the immune system and inflammation, so patients are more prone to infection. Other effects include high blood sugar, high blood pressure, fluid retention, weight gain, moon face, thinning of bones and stomach irritation. Steroids cause raised blood pressure (not low, so A is wrong) and raised blood sugar (not low, so B is wrong), and hair loss (D) is not a typical effect.

questions.text: Drugs used in management of a patient with fluid retention include:
questions.explanation: Lasix (B) is correct because Lasix (furosemide) is a loop diuretic that removes excess fluid through the kidneys, used for oedema from heart failure, kidney or liver disease. Piriton (A) is an antihistamine, paracetamol (C) is a painkiller and fever reducer, and losartan (D) is a blood pressure drug (not a diuretic, though it may reduce fluid indirectly).

questions.text: HCA KK is making a phone call. This level of communication is:
questions.explanation: Interpersonal (C) is correct because a phone call is communication between two people. Intrapersonal (B) is communication within yourself (self-talk), transpersonal (A) is communication involving a spiritual or higher power, and impersonal (D) is not a level of communication in this classification.

questions.text: The stage of group development where members assign meaning to what they have done is:
questions.explanation: Adjourning (D) is correct because in the final stage the group completes its task and members reflect on what they have achieved and what it meant, before the group disbands. Storming (A) is conflict, norming (B) is developing rules and cooperation, and performing (C) is working effectively to reach the goal.

questions.text: The stage of therapeutic relationship where HCA and the client focus on solving problems and accomplishing goals is:
questions.explanation: Working (C) is correct because in the working stage the HCA and client carry out the plan, solve problems and achieve goals. Preorientation (A) is the preparation before meeting the client, orientation (B) is meeting, building trust and setting goals, and termination (D) is ending the relationship.
